title: The Garden Club Feels More Like a Neighborhood Hangout Than a Dispensary
summary: The Garden Club opened in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, in 2026 after three years of legal battles. Its founders built a dispensary around a fireplace, local collaborations, and a happy staff.
body_markdown:
**What happens when a dispensary pays its staff for creative side projects, hosts full-moon parties, and serves Chicago-style hot dogs on Wednesdays that guests can eat by a cozy fireplace?**


You get[The Garden Club](https://www.instagram.com/thegardenclub.bk/?hl=en) , a woman- and minority-owned dispensary at 227 Smith Street in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn. Its founders opened it in 2026 after three years of legal battles and lost locations, and they run it around a curated small-batch menu and a goal of building the happiest dispensary workforce in the world. One that the community wants to show up to, for more than just the weed.


*The outside of The Garden Club in Carroll Garden, New York City*


Alexandria "Dizzy" Alcala (CEO), Erica Diener (CMO), and Matthew Keisoglu (COO) founded the company in 2023 and opened the shop in 2026 in its sole market in New York


According to Dizzy, customers gave the store its unofficial slogan: it feels like a hug. For New York brands, that matters because a shop built for lingering gives a product more time in front of a shopper, and The Garden Club curates its shelves with the same care it gives its design.


The Garden Club CMO Erica Diener on the left, The Garden Club CEO Alexandria "Dizzy" Alcala


## **The Garden Club at a Glance**


- **Founded:** 2023 (opened 2026)
- **Founders:** Alexandria "Dizzy" Alcala (CEO), Erica Diener (CMO), Matthew Keisoglu (COO)
- **Headquarters:** 227 Smith Street, Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, NY 11231
- **Ownership:** Woman- and minority-owned, self-funded, no outside investors
- **Hours:** 10 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily
- **Instagram:**[@thegardenclub.bk](https://www.instagram.com/thegardenclub.bk/)


## **Three Years, Several Lost Locations, One Shop**


Dizzy came to The Garden Club from medical cannabis, retail, and drug-policy advocacy. Erica came from cultivation, hydroponics, cannabis technology, and brand development. Together they saw a chance to help build a legal industry around a plant that had historically been used to criminalize Black and Hispanic communities.


They underestimated the work. Opening took three years, several legal battles, lost locations, and the founders' life savings. Nobody outside the company funded it.


"I got into cannabis because I believed in its potential to change an industry, and ended up falling in love with its potential to bring a neighborhood together," says Dizzy, CEO of The Garden Club.


## **A Shop Designed to Make People Stay**


The shop has a fireplace, plenty of character, and none of the fluorescent lighting that defines most dispensaries. Diener, the CMO, describes the design theme as "1950s Gen Z," telling the[Red Hook Star-Revue](https://www.star-revue.com/a-new-star-revue-feature/) , "Bold with bright colors, but also, kind of classic."


Inside The Garden Club in Carroll Gardens New York City


The team's stated principles shape the floor as much as the decor: budtenders answer questions and recommend with care, every guest gets a judgment-free conversation, and the shop sources, hires, and partners locally under the motto "Brooklyn First, NY Always." One of the three owners is almost always in the store, which should be much more common across the industry.


"We figured if cannabis is supposed to make people feel good, the place you buy it should probably do the same," Dizzy says.


## **What Sits on The Garden Club Shelf?**


The Garden Club curates small-batch flower grown and harvested in New York, limited-drop releases, and thoughtfully dosed edibles.[Danny Danko](https://www.instagram.com/dannydankoht/) , a former cultivation editor at *High Times* , leads menu curation and inventory management, according to the Star-Revue.


With[C.O.D. reporting now in Metrc](https://www.metrc.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/NY_IB_XXXX-Cash-on-Delivery_DRAFT-2-2.pdf) , The Garden Club is a store where small brands can still compete for, gain, and maintain shelf space against larger competitors.


A new line of exclusive Garden Club gear is in progress. The company is also working with resident artists at[Clayhouse](https://www.clayhousebrooklyn.com/) , the neighboring ceramics studio, on handmade pipes, ashtrays, and rolling trays sold only at the shop.


## **Events, Neighbors, and Chicago-Style Hot Dogs**


The store gives people reasons to show up. It hosts[full-moon parties](https://partiful.com/u/G3sbLl0PM6gnfWw0IvEO) with local creatives, a drag night called “Drag Me To The Garden,” and even car meets.


On Weed Wiener Wednesdays, a $60 purchase earns a Chicago-style hot dog from[Bobbi’s Italian Beef](https://www.instagram.com/bobbis_italianbeef/?hl=en) , a neighboring restaurant across the street. Dizzy grew up in Chicago, so she calls that one personal.


The neighborhood returns the favor. The cheese shop next door,[Lea Fromages](https://www.instagram.com/leafromages/?hl=en) , drops off leftover sandwiches at closing, and merchants on the block trade change and favors all day.


## **How The Garden Club Feels Like Neighbors to its Customers**


Dizzy talked about one story in particular that still sits with her.


A customer came in with her husband while she was undergoing a biopsy and was frightened. Human-to-human, Dizzy talked with her about how far medicine has come, early detection, and pleaded with her to come back after the biopsy. The customer came back a few weeks later to say the conversation had helped, that it mattered.


In another story Dizzy shared, a customer came in days after losing her husband. Dizzy brought her into the back room, and they cried together. That customer still visits every few weeks.


Customers outside of The Garden Club dispensary


"It's funny, because we sell cannabis, but some of the most meaningful things that happen in our shop have absolutely nothing to do with weed," Dizzy says.


## **The Happiest Staff in Cannabis**


The team includes artists, knitters, tarot readers, writers, and other creatives, and the founders encourage all of them to bring their whole selves to work. The Garden Club pays staff for creative projects outside their regular roles and is exploring plans to share its financial success with the staff as the business grows.


"Our goal is to create the happiest dispensary workforce in the world," Dizzy says. "We want the warmth people feel when they walk into The Garden Club to be a reflection of how the people working there feel, too."


## **What's Next**


The Clayhouse collaboration is the next product launch, and the full-moon parties continue to anchor the event calendar. The founders keep the same priorities as they grow: education, community, creativity, and taking care of people.


Brooklyn shoppers can visit The Garden Club at 227 Smith Street, seven days a week.


## **Frequently Asked Questions About The Garden Club**


### **What is The Garden Club?**


The Garden Club is a woman- and minority-owned, New York State-licensed dispensary at 227 Smith Street in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, founded in 2023 and opened in 2026.


### **Who founded The Garden Club?**


Alexandria "Dizzy" Alcala (CEO), Erica Diener (CMO), and Matthew Keisoglu (COO) founded The Garden Club.


### **Where is The Garden Club located?**


The Garden Club is located at 227 Smith Street in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, New York, and is open daily from 10 a.m. to 11 p.m.


### **What does The Garden Club sell?**


The Garden Club sells small-batch New York flower, limited-drop releases, and edibles, plus handmade pipes, ashtrays, and rolling trays made with Clayhouse artists.


### **What are Weed Wiener Wednesdays at The Garden Club?**


On Weed Wiener Wednesdays, customers who spend $60 at The Garden Club get a Chicago-style hot dog from[Bobbi’s Italian Beef](https://www.instagram.com/bobbis_italianbeef/?hl=en) , a neighboring restaurant.


### **Does The Garden Club host events?**


Yes. The Garden Club hosts full-moon parties with local creatives, a drag night, and car meets.
